BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). 3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Candlestick charts can render incorrectly or fail outright when data is mapped through `series.encode`, particularly in layouts that are not the simplest default case.
6

8	
9	  Candlestick rendering should honor `series.encode` correctly across supported layouts so encoded dimensions still produce a valid candlestick chart.
10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals
12	
13	  A candlestick series driven by `series.encode` renders with the expected orientation and geometry instead of crashing or misplacing the candle bodies and whiskers.
14	
15	  '

input.summary: Candlestick layout/render hard-codes the cartesian orientation (`cDimIdx = 0`, `vDimIdx = 1`, `point[1]`, vertical-only large path), so any non-default layout — i.e. `layout: 'vertical'` / a category `yAxis`, including series driven by `series.encode` — resolves the wrong data dimensions, bails out of the layout stage and then throws (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'sign')` in candlestickVisual, and `reading 'length'` in `LargeBoxPath.buildPath` in large mode). Fix by deriving the constant/value dimension indices from `seriesModel.get('layout')` (exactly as `boxplotLayout`/`BoxplotView` already do) and by making the init-animation baseline and the large-mode point buffer orientation-aware.
steps: REPRODUCTION (already verified, no source edits): with `xAxis: {}, yAxis: {type:'category'}, series: [{type:'candlestick', encode: {y: 0, x: [1,2,3,4]}, data: [...]}]`, `chart.setOption` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'sign')` at /workspace/src/chart/candlestick/candlestickVisual.ts:68 (`data.getItemLayout(dataIndex).sign`). Root cause: /workspace/src/chart/candlestick/candlestickLayout.ts:70 `if (cDimI < 0 || vDimsI.length < 4) { return; }` fires, because for a vertical layout `data.mapDimensionsAll('y')` === `['base']` (length 1) and `data.mapDimension('x')` === `'open'`. In large mode the same bail-out leaves `largePoints` unset and /workspace/src/chart/candlestick/CandlestickView.ts:351 throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')`. `seriesModel.get('layout')` is reliably `'horizontal'`/`'vertical'` here because /workspace/src/chart/helper/whiskerBoxCommon.ts:82-94 always writes `option.layout` in `getInitialData` (verified at runtime).

STEP 4 — /workspace/src/chart/candlestick/CandlestickView.ts, update the three `createNormalBox` call sites to pass `constDim`. In `_renderNormal` (starts line 93), add after line 97/before line 99 (i.e. next to `const needsClip = seriesModel.get('clip', true);`):
```ts
        const constDim = seriesModel.get('layout') === 'horizontal' ? 1 : 0;
```
(this matches /workspace/src/chart/boxplot/BoxplotView.ts:49). Then change line 118 `const el = createNormalBox(itemLayout, newIdx, true);` -> `const el = createNormalBox(itemLayout, newIdx, constDim, true);`, and line 144 `el = createNormalBox(itemLayout, newIdx);` -> `el = createNormalBox(itemLayout, newIdx, constDim);`. In `_incrementalRenderNormal` (lines 187-202) add the same `const constDim = seriesModel.get('layout') === 'horizontal' ? 1 : 0;` next to line 189 and change line 194 `const el = createNormalBox(itemLayout, dataIndex);` -> `const el = createNormalBox(itemLayout, dataIndex, constDim);` (`seriesModel` is already a parameter of both methods).

STEP 6 — /workspace/src/chart/candlestick/CandlestickView.ts, `createLarge` (lines 364-404). After `const largePoints = data.getLayout('largePoints');` (line 371) add:
```ts
    const isVertical = seriesModel.get('layout') === 'vertical';
```
and pass `__isVertical: isVertical,` alongside `__sign` in all three `new LargeBoxPath({...})` constructions (lines 373-377 `__sign: 1`, 379-383 `__sign: -1`, 385-389 `__sign: 0`). Verified at runtime that zrender copies these `__`-prefixed opts onto the element, same as the existing `__sign`.

STEP 7 (defensive, optional but recommended) — /workspace/src/chart/candlestick/CandlestickView.ts `createLarge`: after reading `largePoints`, `if (!largePoints) { return; }`. And /workspace/src/chart/candlestick/candlestickVisual.ts line 68 `const sign = data.getItemLayout(dataIndex).sign;` -> `const layout = data.getItemLayout(dataIndex); if (!layout) { continue; } const sign = layout.sign;`. These stop the hard crash if the layout stage still bails out (e.g. a user `encode` that supplies fewer than 4 value dimensions), turning it into a silently-skipped item rather than a thrown exception.

STEP 8 — Regression test. There is currently no `test/ut/spec/chart/` directory, but /workspace/test/ut/jest.config.cjs `testMatch` already includes `'**/spec/chart/**/*.test.ts'`, so create /workspace/test/ut/spec/chart/candlestick.test.ts (Apache license header required — see /workspace/test/ut/spec/series/custom.test.ts for the template; import `createChart` from `../../core/utHelper`). Cover: (1) vertical layout via category `yAxis` + `encode: {y: 0, x: [1,2,3,4]}` — `expect(() => chart.setOption(option)).not.toThrow()` and `expect(data.getItemLayout(0)).toBeTruthy()`; (2) assert orientation: for the vertical case the four body points share two distinct x values and `ends[4][1] === ends[6][1]` (whisker is horizontal, constant y), whereas for the horizontal case `ends[4][0] === ends[6][0]`; (3) `layout: 'vertical'` with two value axes; (4) large mode (`large: true, largeThreshold: 10`) vertical — `data.getLayout('largePoints')` is defined and `points[1]` is the y coordinate. Run with `npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs --coverage=false`.

STEP 9 (optional) — Visual test page. Add /workspace/test/candlestick-vertical.html modelled on /workspace/test/candlestick.html (or /workspace/test/candlestick-large3.html, which already uses `encode: {x: 0, y: [1, 4, 3, 2]}`), with a `yAxis: {type: 'category'}` + `encode: {y: 0, x: [1,2,3,4]}` case and a large-mode vertical case, so the fixed orientation is visible in `npm run test:visual`.
input.risks: No new public option is needed: `layout?: LayoutOrient` already exists on `CandlestickSeriesOption` (/workspace/src/chart/candlestick/CandlestickSeries.ts:74) with default `layout: null` (line 111), and `whiskerBoxCommon.getInitialData` (/workspace/src/chart/helper/whiskerBoxCommon.ts:82-94) always normalizes it to 'horizontal'/'vertical' before the layout stage runs — do NOT change that default or the mixin, since boxplot shares it. Verification done: I copied src+test to /tmp/sc, applied exactly the edits above, and the full unit suite passed (25 suites / 192 tests) plus my ad-hoc vertical/encode/large cases; the /workspace tree was left untouched (`git status --porcelain` clean). Remaining risks: (a) `makeBrushRect` produces a negative `height` in horizontal layout today (pre-existing, brush selection on candlestick) — the fix does not change horizontal output at all, so do not "fix" it here; (b) `createLarge` pushes only `elP, elN` into `progressiveEls` and sets `incremental` only on those two, omitting `elDoji` — pre-existing bug, out of scope; (c) `CandlestickSeriesModel.getShadowDim()` returns `'open'` for the dataZoom slider shadow, which assumes a horizontal orientation — out of scope for this requirement; (d) other requirement files in /workspace/requirements do not touch candlestick, so no cross-requirement conflict expected.
